title.turn_play: Each turn you play one agent from your hand for one action: sail, march, found a colony, gather, work, build, trade, hire, win over a Founding Father.
title.round_ends: Each round ends with an event and the King’s tax. Refusing it sends redcoats to the Royal Army.
title.15_bells: At 15 bells or after round 10 comes the War of Independence. The least rebellious governor sides with the King; the others defend their colonies.
title.colonies_hold: Colonies that hold, bells, agents, gold, buildings and Fathers score points. Keep at least one colony to win.

guide.govern_colony: You govern a colony of a European power in the New World, from {firstYear} to {v}. Explore, found up to {max} colonies, trade, grow.
guide.game_ends: The game ends with the War of Independence, when someone has {bells} {bells2} or after round {max}. The least rebellious governor sides with the King; the others defend their colonies.
guide.win_hold: To win you must hold at least one colony after the war and have the most victory points {vp}. Nobody holds one: the Crown wins.
guide.draw_up: Draw up to {size} agents. An empty deck is refilled by shuffling your discard.
guide.turn_player: In turn, each player plays one agent for one action. Passing ends your round; the others go on until all have passed.
guide.top_event: Then the top event happens, and the King asks for his tax.
guide.recruit_play: Recruit: play an agent on the Europe deck and spend crosses {crosses}, at least the round number. Look at as many agents from the top, take one to your discard; the rest go to the bottom.
guide.agent_take: Any agent can take any action; its talent adds where it fits (a sailor sails further, a planter grows more crops, a soldier fights better).
guide.education_decides: Education 👒 / 📖 / 🎓 decides which buildings an agent can work in and what can be taught.
guide.criminal_slave: The criminal and the slave may only produce (and support in battle).
guide.played_agent: A played agent goes to your discard.
guide.one_action: One action moves your ship {ship} and your pawn {pawn}: {points} points between them, in any order. Ocean and grassland cost 1, forest, desert and tundra 2; mountains take all that remain.
guide.moving_clouds: Moving into the clouds explores ({explore} point): a 3×3 part of the map appears, with its land, native villages, ruins and wrecks.
guide.infantry_rides: The pawn rides aboard. To land or board, it moves into the target cell and pays its cost.
guide.hold_places: The hold has {size} places: one per resource kind, one for the pawn, one per damage. Loading and unloading at your colony cost {cargo} point.
guide.not_edge: not on the map’s outer edge,
guide.edge_map: The edge of the map is Europe. Ruins (pawn) and wrecks (ship) give a card with a choice when first entered.
guide.infantry_founds: Your pawn founds a colony on its own land cell: {edge}not next to a colony or village, with sea leading to Europe. The first is free, the others cost {value} {v}.
guide.build_timber: Build with timber: up to {max} buildings, one of each. Work in a building with an agent educated enough: workshops turn crops into goods, schools retrain agents, docks work the sea, and so on.
guide.warehouse_resources: Warehouse: {base} resources (more with the warehouse building); the excess is lost at the end of your turn. Your warehouse, buildings and Fathers serve all your colonies.
guide.supply_1: Supply: 1 food, draw 1 agent. Exchange: discard 2 agents, draw 1.
guide.ship_map: With your ship on the map’s edge you can act in Europe.
guide.trade_sell: Trade: sell your hold at today’s prices (up to {maxPrice}). Sales fill a demand track as long as the number of players; each time it fills, that price falls by 1.
guide.hire_buy: Hire: buy up to {max} different agents from the pier with gold, or clear the pier for new ones.
guide.propaganda_take: Propaganda: take up to {maxFathers} Founding Fathers from the salon, paying bells; at most {max} in all.
guide.repair_remove: Repair: remove a damage from your ship.
guide.villages_appear: Villages appear as the map is explored. A tribe’s hostility {hostility} runs from 0 to {maxHostility}, shared by its villages.
guide.next_village: Next to a village: give goods (hostility falls), preach (pay crosses equal to hostility, gain a native agent), attack, or make an alliance at low hostility.
guide.events_activate: Events activate villages: a friendly one gives food to the nearest colony, a hostile one raids it.
guide.attack_neighbouring: Attack a neighbouring cell with an agent that has a 🗡️ for your token (pawn or ship). Both sides then add cards from hand in secret.
guide.beaten_token: A beaten token goes to Europe; tokens are never destroyed. Against a colony each success takes a resource or a building. Colonies can only be taken in the war.
guide.one_event: One event a round, from a shuffled deck: storms, wars, prices, the King’s demands. At most {max} are seen.
guide.ruins_wrecks: Ruins and wrecks offer choices with costs and dice: gold, agents, cargo, or trouble.
guide.begins_after: It begins after the tax of a round in which someone reaches {bells} {bells2}, or after round {max}.
guide.governor_fewest: The governor with the fewest bells becomes the loyalist and fights for the King (only with {loyalistFrom} or more players; otherwise the Royal Army attacks alone).
guide.governor_fewest2: The governor with the fewest bells becomes the loyalist and fights for the King (not in solo).
guide.king_s: The Royal Army: every redcoat collected, plus 1 per hostile village and the King’s tactic. Its redcoats are dealt to the patriots’ colonies; each attacks with {refStrength}.
guide.patriots_defend: Patriots defend in secret with military agents, militia (1 {bells} each), mercenaries ({mercenaryGold} {gold} each) and allies ({allyCubes} each). A colony attacked by more than it can hold rolls dice; any success takes it.
guide.patriot_per: Every colony held after the war, defended or taken in it: {patriotColony} {vp}, for everyone. Every {bellsPerPoint} {bells} left: {perBell} {vp}, except for the loyalist.
guide.everybody_1: Everybody: 1 {vp} per {agentsPerPoint} agents, 1 {vp} per {goldPerPoint} {gold}, {building} {vp} per building, {fathers} {vp} per Father, and the cards’ own bonuses.
guide.ties_go: Ties go to gold, then to the number of agents.
guide.gold_bells: {gold} gold · {bells} bells (rebellion) · {crosses} crosses (faith) · {king} the Royal Army · {vp} victory points

tutorial.outlined_edge: The outlined edge of the map is Europe: your ship comes from there, and goes back there to trade. Click a cell on the edge to choose where your ship starts.
tutorial.icons_top: The icons at the top of a picture are the agent’s talent, a bonus where the action fits: +1 {move}{ship} sails a cell further, +1 {food} gathers more food, +2 {power} fights better. Two limits: only an agent with {power} can attack, and the criminal and the slave can only gather.
tutorial.drop_agent: Drop an agent on the sea to sail: one action gives the ship {points} movement points, 1 for each sea cell. The clouds hide unknown land; sailing into them reveals a new part of the map. Sail into the clouds now.
tutorial.infantry_rides: Your pawn {pawn} rides aboard. Sail along a coast, then drop an agent on a land cell with a yellow flag: the pawn lands and founds a colony there. The first one is free. Grassland and forest by the sea are good land.
tutorial.colony_works: A colony works its own cell and the cells around it. Drop an agent on one to gather what it yields: {food} {timber} {crops} {silver}. It goes to your warehouse, beside the hand. The warehouse holds {base}; the rest is lost.
tutorial.round_buttons: The round buttons at the bottom open two boards. Colony: build with {timber}, then put agents to work in the buildings; a building needs enough education, the mark before an agent’s name. Europe: sell what your ship carries, hire agents, gain Founding Fathers. Selling, hiring and repair need your ship on the edge of the map; Fathers do not.
tutorial.native_villages: Native villages appear as you explore. Next to one you can give goods to calm its tribe, preach with {crosses} to win a native agent, make an alliance while it is calm, or attack it. Each tribe’s hostility {hostility} runs from 0 to {maxHostility}: calm villages bring your colonies food, angry ones raid them.
tutorial.done_want: When you have done what you want, Pass. When everybody has passed, the round ends: an event happens, the King asks for his tax, and you draw back up to {size} agents.
tutorial.know_enough: You know enough to play. Advice, beside Pass, suggests a move when you are unsure, and F1 opens the rules at any time. The tips turn off now; Options turns them back on. Good luck, governor!

event.sugar_act: Crops fall by 1. Players with crops gain 1 {bells}, and may sell crops to smugglers: 1 {king} for each.
event.silver_fleet: Silver falls by 1. The first player may take a corsair for 5 {gold}. The player with most silver pays 2 {gold} for each, or gains 1 {bells} and adds 1 {king}.
event.seven_years_war: Goods and silver rise by 1. Every agent with {power} on the pier is replaced. Players may sell up to 3 top agents for 6 {gold} each, adding 1 {king} each.
event.the_great_awakening: Chapels give 2 {crosses}, churches 4. Players secretly give up {crosses}: every 4 remove 1 {king}.
event.smallpox_epidemic: Timber rises by 1. Every settlement loses 1 population. The pier is replaced.
event.stamp_act: Goods rise by 1. Town hall or newspaper gives 1 {bells}. Pay 2 {gold} per building or add 1 {king} for each unpaid one.
event.atlantic_storms: All prices rise by 1. Ships outside Europe lose their cargo, or take damage if empty. The player with fewest colonies finds 2 {goods}.
event.pontiacs_rebellion: All settlements with hostility 4 or 5 raid. 1 {king} per player.
event.broken_treaties: Alliances at hostility 3 or more end. All settlements with hostility 4 or 5 raid.
event.black_market: Goods fall by 1. Players may sell anything at 1 less. 2 {king} per smuggler.
event.starving_time: Food rises by 1. Calm settlements give 1 {food} to the nearest colony. Every colony eats 1 {food}, or its owner loses the top agent.
event.prison_ships: Timber falls by 1. The first player may take a criminal. 1 {king} per player.
event.common_sense: The salon is replaced. 2 {king} per 5 {bells} of all players.
event.industrial_boom: Goods fall, crops rise by 1. Players may build a blacksmith shop or factory for 2 {timber}. The player with most goods pays 3 {gold} or adds 1 {king}.
event.salem_witch_trials: The player with most {crosses} accuses someone, who loses a learned agent or gains 5 {crosses}. 1 {king} per player.
event.mutiny: Silver rises by 1. Pay 2 {gold} for each agent with {power}, or lose it: 2 {king} each.
event.sacred_forest: Timber rises by 1. The player with most timber pays 1 {goods} or 5 {gold}, or all natives grow angrier. Hostile settlements raid.
event.el_dorado_rumors: Silver falls by 1. Players may sell up to 3 top agents for 5 {gold} each. 2 {king} per player.
event.slave_rebellion: Crops rise by 1. Pay 2 {gold} per slave or lose them: 1 {king} each.
event.treaty_of_paris: Crops and goods return to their first price. Hostility falls by 1. The first player may take a soldier for 5 {gold}.
event.the_boston_tea_party: Goods rise by 1. Pay 2 {gold} per {goods}, or throw them away for 1 {bells} and 2 {king} each. 1 {king} per player.
event.pirate_blockade: Goods rise by 1. Ships outside Europe pay 3 {gold}, or take damage and lose their cargo: 2 {king} each.

tutorial.welcome: You are the governor of {nation} in the New World. Each round you play agents to explore, found colonies, gather, build and trade; {goal}. These tips show one thing at a time and move on when you have done it.
tutorial.goal_solo: keep a colony to the end to win
tutorial.goal_vp: the most victory points {vp} at the end win
tutorial.agents: These cards are your agents. On your turn you play one of them for one action{others}. Any agent can take any action. Pick one up (drag it, or click it) and every place it can act lights up.
tutorial.tax: At the end of this round the King asks for {gold} gold. Pay{pay}, or refuse: a refusal {bells}adds {n, plural, one {# redcoat} other {# redcoats}} to the Royal Army {king}. Bells measure your rebellion and pay for Founding Fathers.
tutorial.war: The game ends with a war, after the round in which {who} {n} {bells}, or after round {max}. {loyalist}The Royal Army {king}, every redcoat collected plus one per hostile village, attacks {whose}. Defend with agents with {power}, militia paid in bells and mercenaries paid in gold; a colony attacked by a stronger force falls.
tutorial.loyalist: The governor with the fewest bells joins the King; the others fight for independence.
tutorial.score: {rule} Victory points {vp}: {colony} per colony held, {bell} per {bpp} {bells} left, {building} per building, {fathers} per Father, 1 per {per} {gold} and 1 per {agents} agents.{ally} The emblems at the top right show everyone’s points so far: click the points to see where they come from; an action that gains points shows them with the same sign.
tutorial.rule_solo: Hold at least one colony through the war and you win; lose them all and the Crown wins.
tutorial.rule: Only a governor who holds a colony after the war can win, with the most victory points; if nobody holds one, the Crown wins.
tutorial.ally: The King’s ally scores {n} per colony, those taken included, and nothing for bells.
guide.tax: Tax by round: {track} {gold}. Pay{pay}, or refuse: +{n} {n, plural, one {redcoat} other {redcoats}} to the Royal Army (solo +{solo}, 2 players +{two}){bells}. Who cannot pay must refuse.
guide.produce: Produce: take 1 resource from the colony’s cell or an empty neighbour; a bonus icon on the cell adds 1. Forest {forest}, grassland {crops}, mountains {silver}, ocean {food}; desert and tundra give nothing.
guide.forest: {timber} ({crops} fur only with its bonus or a trapper)
guide.strength: Strength is the number of cards plus their 🗡️ and bonuses. If the attack is stronger, roll as many dice as the difference: each {faces} is a success. Any win gives +{n} {bells}.
top.vp_note: Only a governor who holds a colony after the war can win.
flavor.father.christopher_columbus: 1451–1506. The man who set out to reach the Indies and found America.
flavor.father.jakob_fugger: 1459–1525. The richest banker of his age, who financed the conquest.
flavor.father.ponce_de_leon: 1474–1521. Seeker of the fountain of youth.
flavor.father.bartolome_de_las_casas: 1484–1566. Defender of the rights of the Indians.
flavor.father.juan_de_sepulveda: 1494–1573. Advocate of the enslavement of the Indians.
flavor.father.walter_raleigh: 1552–1618. Champion of the colonization of America.
flavor.father.john_smith: 1580–1631. One of the founders of Jamestown.
flavor.father.squanto: 1585–1622. A Patuxet who helped the colonists survive.
flavor.father.john_rolfe: 1585–1622. Tobacco planter in Virginia and husband of Pocahontas.
flavor.father.thomas_hooker: 1586–1647. Puritan founder of the Connecticut colony.
flavor.father.william_bradford: 1590–1657. Pilgrim Father and founder of Plymouth colony.
flavor.father.pocahontas: 1596–1617. Daughter of the Powhatan chief, who helped the English.
flavor.father.roger_williams: 1603–1683. Baptist founder of the Rhode Island colony.
flavor.father.john_eliot: 1604–1690. Translator of the Bible into the Algonquian language.
flavor.father.michiel_de_ruyter: 1607–1676. Admiral of a string of great victories.
flavor.father.robert_de_la_salle: 1643–1687. Explorer of the Great Lakes and the Mississippi.
flavor.father.paul_revere: 1734–1818. Hero of the American War of Independence.
flavor.father.thomas_jefferson: 1743–1826. Author of the Declaration of Independence, third President of the United States.
flavor.father.olaudah_equiano: 1745–1797. A freed slave and a leader of the movement to end slavery.
flavor.father.thaddeus_kosciuszko: 1746–1817. Military engineer and general of the Continental Army.
flavor.father.simon_bolivar: 1783–1830. Leader of the wars of independence of the Spanish colonies.
flavor.father.benedict_arnold: 1741–1801. General of the Continental Army who betrayed the patriots.
flavor.event.sugar_act: The mother country lays crushing duties on the sweet gold of the New World. Smuggling becomes a point of honour for every colonist.
flavor.event.silver_fleet: Galleons laden with silver make ready to sail for Europe. The King wants his share.
flavor.event.seven_years_war: The Old World is ablaze with war. The Crown demands recruits from the colonies, and gunsmiths raise the price of muskets and cannon.
flavor.event.the_great_awakening: Wandering preachers draw crowds to the squares. People seek the salvation of their souls and forget worldly cares and ringing coin.
flavor.event.smallpox_epidemic: Death came on the ships from Europe. It spares neither the colonists nor, above all, the native peoples of this land.
flavor.event.stamp_act: Parliament has decreed it: from now on every printed paper, licence and diploma bears a stamp duty.
flavor.event.atlantic_storms: Savage hurricanes toss ships like splinters. Word from the mother country is cut off, and the ports fill with rotting goods.
flavor.event.pontiacs_rebellion: A great chief unites the tribes to drive the Europeans out. The forts prepare for a siege.
flavor.event.broken_treaties: One careless word, one wounded pride, and yesterday’s allies take up arms.
flavor.event.black_market: In the shadow of harbour taverns, deals are struck that the King’s tax collectors never hear of. Smuggling thrives.
flavor.event.starving_time: The rivers have frozen and the stores run low. The colonies’ survival rests on the mercy of the natives and on one another.
flavor.event.prison_ships: The mother country clears its streets, shipping convicts, thieves and debtors off to certain death in the colonies.
flavor.event.common_sense: Pamphlets calling for liberty pass from tavern to tavern, stirring the people to revolt.
flavor.event.industrial_boom: Looms hum and mills turn. The colonies are no longer just a source of raw goods for the Old World.
flavor.event.salem_witch_trials: A wave of superstition sweeps the colonies. Neighbours inform on neighbours, and juries will send to the gallows anyone the crowd points at.
flavor.event.mutiny: The pay is six months late. The soldiers threaten to turn their bayonets on their own officers unless they are paid.
flavor.event.sacred_forest: The woodcutters have gone too far and desecrated a native shrine. The air smells of blood and smoke.
flavor.event.el_dorado_rumors: People whisper of golden cities lost in the mountains. A fever for easy riches grips the colonies.
flavor.event.slave_rebellion: The chains are broken. The oppressed rise on the plantations and demand their freedom, weapons in hand.
flavor.event.treaty_of_paris: Officials in powdered wigs have redrawn the map of the world. A long-awaited, if fragile, respite has come.
flavor.event.the_boston_tea_party: The people are tired of the mother country’s levies. Chests of the King’s tea fly into the harbour.
flavor.event.pirate_blockade: Pirates have choked the trade routes. Governors must arm their merchant ships at their own cost.
flavor.ruin.natives_ambush: The ruins were a lure. Poisoned arrows fly from the undergrowth.
flavor.ruin.predators_lair: You have woken a pack of wild beasts that made their den in an ancient temple.
flavor.ruin.golden_city: El Dorado was only a legend after all, yet you find plenty of gold in an ancient, abandoned city.
flavor.ruin.silver_mines: An ancient mine, perhaps a source of precious ore.
flavor.ruin.survivor: You have found a man from a lost expedition. He knows this land like the back of his hand.
flavor.ruin.abandoned_fort: Someone has tried to live here before. Sound log cabins and a few tools remain.
flavor.ruin.hidden_granaries: Stores of maize hidden in caves, left by generations past.
flavor.ruin.smugglers_cave: Someone hid the fruits of their unlawful labour here.
flavor.ruin.mere_rumors: The tales of a rich burial were false.
flavor.ruin.native_burial: A burial ground of the local people.
flavor.ruin.desecrated_burial: The grave of a native warrior has already been opened and plundered.
flavor.ruin.sacred_totem_circle: They say whoever disturbs them will bring the wrath of the spirits upon himself.
flavor.ruin.guide: A native guide comes to meet you. He will show you a secret path to the tomb, but not for nothing.
flavor.ruin.warrior_burial: Among the bones lies finely made warrior’s armour.
flavor.ruin.bandeirante_tracks: You have come upon the tracks of European adventurers who were here before you.
flavor.ruin.stone_wall: The burial is sealed behind a stone wall. Getting inside will not be easy.
flavor.ruin.protective_amulet: A golden amulet with the image of some fearsome idol hangs at the entrance.
flavor.ruin.defiled_shrine: The burial was plundered long ago, but something may have survived.
flavor.ruin.lost_tomb: Legend says a mighty chief is buried here.
flavor.ruin.trail_marker: Signs carved into one of the totems point out landmarks.
flavor.wreck.shipwreck: All you find are empty rum barrels.
flavor.wreck.sunken_galleon: A great ship has run onto the reefs. Its holds are bursting with the riches of the New World.
flavor.wreck.man_overboard: A survivor of a shipwreck is found in the water.
flavor.wreck.floating_cargo: Sealed barrels and bales of valuable goods bob in the water.
flavor.wreck.plague_ship: A yellow flag flies over the ship. The crew is dead of fever, but the captain’s strongbox stands open.
flavor.wreck.drifting_frigate: A warship with no crew. The guns are whole and the powder room is full.
flavor.wreck.pirate_ambush: The wreckage was a lure! A brig flying the Jolly Roger rounds the cape.
flavor.wreck.sea_charts: In the dead captain’s cabin you find exact charts of the currents and shoals.
flavor.wreck.smugglers_cache: Valuables are hidden in the coastal caves near the wreck.
flavor.wreck.surviving_crew: Starving sailors in a longboat will swear loyalty to you if you save them.
flavor.wreck.treacherous_reefs: As you close in on the wreckage, your ship’s hull grinds on hidden rocks.
flavor.wreck.slave_ship: Captive natives are found in the hold of a ship run aground.
flavor.wreck.gutted_hull: Someone was here before you. Only bare planks and empty barrels are left.
flavor.wreck.calm_seas: The ship is caught in a dead calm.
flavor.wreck.capricious_official: A high-ranking passenger demands more room for his cabin.
flavor.wreck.lost_relic: The captain’s log tells of a Christian relic on board that sank with the ship.
flavor.wreck.message_in_a_bottle_1: A captain’s tender letter to his beloved.
flavor.wreck.message_in_a_bottle_2: A sailor angrily brands the King a tyrant and calls for revolt.
flavor.wreck.message_in_a_bottle_3: The letter holds deep thoughts on the meaning of life, freedom and duty.
flavor.wreck.rich_reefs: The wreckage points to reefs rich in pearls.
